hypothesis: Across 200 seeded simulated trials per condition (n=30 per arm, noise SD 1.2 ohms, minimum effect 5 ohms), the analysis concludes SUPPORTS in at least 80% of trials with a true -6.5 ohm effect and in at most 5% of null trials.
limitations: Simulated Gaussian data: this characterizes the analysis pipeline, not any physical, acoustic or biological effect.
One effect size, one noise level and one sample size; error rates at other operating points are unmeasured.
Seeds are consecutive integers; the simulator's RNG quality bounds independence between trials.

metrics.description: SUPPORTS rate with a true -6.5 ohm effect.
metrics.name: detection_rate

metrics.description: INCONCLUSIVE rate with the true effect.
metrics.name: effect_inconclusive_rate

metrics.description: REFUTES rate with the true effect.
metrics.name: effect_refutes_rate

metrics.description: SUPPORTS rate with no effect (false support).
metrics.name: false_supports_rate

procedure: Design one CIRCLE manifest (alpha 0.05, min n 20, effect-size threshold 0.5, minimum effect 5 ohms, expected decrease).
For 200 seeds (seed + i) simulate a trial with a -6.5 ohm active effect; for 200 disjoint seeds (seed + 1,000,000 + i) simulate a null trial.
Analyse every trial with the unchanged run_deterministic_analysis and count conclusions per condition.
question: How often does the pre-registered CIRCLE analysis conclude SUPPORTS when a simulated effect beyond the minimum is present, versus when there is no effect at all?
rationale: The reviewed simulation workflow reports SUPPORTS/REFUTES/INCONCLUSIVE from one trial. The analysis's detection rate and false-support rate under known ground truth have not been measured; this calibrates it.
title: CIRCLE analysis error rates on seeded simulated controls
